title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck works in the profinite completion of the extension 1 -> Π̂_{0,3} -> Ĝ -> S_3 -> 1. Here Π̂_{0,3} is the free profinite group on loops l_0, l_1 around 0 and 1, and Ĝ is essentially \widehat{PSL_2(Z)}, with Γ(2) ≅ F_2 and PSL_2(Z)/Γ(2) = S_3. Ĝ is generated by Π̂_{0,3}, an involution σ_∞ (swapping 0 and 1) and an order-3 element ρ (permuting 0, 1, ∞ cyclically). He wants all automorphisms u of Ĝ with u(σ_∞) = σ_∞ and u(ρ) = gρ, where gρ must again be a torsion element of order 3. These are the 'u' of the Corollary on the previous page, a forerunner of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group. Note that γ = (p-1)/2 plays the role of m = (λ-1)/2 in Drinfeld's notation (λ ∈ Ẑ*).

NB (first paragraph). The parameter λ ∈ Π̂_{0,3} is only defined modulo left multiplication by L_0 = l_0^Ẑ. He checks equivariance under λ' = l_0^α λ:
- ξ = λρ(λ)^{-1} becomes ξ' = l_0^α ξ ρ(l_0)^{-α};
- h_0 = ξ^{-1} l_0^γ becomes h_0' = ρ(l_0)^α h_0 l_0^{-α};
- g_0 becomes g_0' = g_0 l_0^{-α}.
So equation (60) for ξ and for ξ' are equivalent. The check is direct, using that l_0 commutes with l_0^γ. The last step needs σ_∞(l_0) and ρ(l_0) to agree, which holds with the normalisation l_1 = ρ(l_0) = σ_∞(l_0).

Procedure ('la démarche la plus claire') for constructing all such u. It is continued on the next page.
1°) Choose ξ ∈ Π̂_{0,3} with (A) ξ ρ(ξ) ρ²(ξ) = 1. This says (ξρ)^3 = 1, i.e. ξρ is again of order 3: a 1-cocycle condition for Z/3 acting on Π̂_{0,3}. By the earlier classification (55)/(56) of order-3 elements, its solutions are of the form (B): ξ = λρ(λ)^{-1} (conjugates of ρ) or ξ = λ l_0^{-1} ρ(λ)^{-1} (the other class). This is in effect a computation of nonabelian H^1(Z/3, Π̂_{0,3}) with two classes.
2°) Find γ ∈ Ẑ with (C) σ_∞(ξ) = l_1^γ ξ^{-1} l_0^γ. This is the condition h_0 σ_∞(h_0) = 1, i.e. a Z/2-cocycle condition, for h_0 = ξ^{-1} l_0^γ. It makes h_0 a coboundary σ_∞(g_0)^{-1} g_0. γ is unique if it exists; one also needs p = 2γ+1 ∈ Ẑ*.
Then (next page) g = σ_∞(g_0) l_1^γ ρ(g_0)^{-1}, and u is defined by u(σ_∞) = σ_∞, u(ρ) = gρ.

In modern terms, these are the 3-cycle ('hexagon') and 2-cycle relations defining (a variant of) GT̂ inside Aut(\widehat{PSL_2(Z)}), each read as a nonabelian cocycle/coboundary condition for Z/3 resp. Z/2, with the exponent m = γ appearing in the 2-cycle step.
errors: The previous page's transcription of (60) reads σ_∞(ξ) = l_1^γ ξ l_0^γ. The derivation σ_∞(ξ)^{-1} l_1^γ ξ^{-1} l_0^γ = 1 gives σ_∞(ξ) = l_1^γ ξ^{-1} l_0^γ, which is what this page writes as (C). Either the earlier transcription or Grothendieck's (60) lacks the inverse.
The NB check g_0' = g_0 l_0^{-α} silently uses σ_∞(l_0) = ρ(l_0) (= l_1). This is true under the standard normalisation but is not stated.
The uniqueness of γ in (C) is asserted without proof. It is plausible: two values would force l_1^{δ} ξ^{-1} l_0^{δ}-type identities in a free profinite group.

ideas.what: Describe automorphisms of the profinite extension Π̂_{0,3}⋊S_3 (≈ \widehat{PSL_2(Z)}) fixing σ_∞ and sending ρ to gρ. Parametrise them by (λ, p) with p = 2γ+1 ∈ Ẑ*.
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT̂ / automorphisms of \widehat{PSL_2(Z)} (genus-0, 4-point level)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1991); PSL_2(Ẑ)-viewpoint in Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Harbater–Schneps (1990s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches the idea; La Longue Marche (1981, circulated) contains related computations

ideas.what: Equation ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ) = 1 solved via nonabelian H^1 of Z/3: ξ = λρ(λ)^{-1} or λ l_0^{-1}ρ(λ)^{-1} (two conjugacy classes of order-3 elements).
ideas.modern_name: 3-cycle (hexagon) relation of GT as a cocycle condition

ideas.what: Condition σ_∞(ξ) = l_1^γ ξ^{-1} l_0^γ with 2γ+1 ∈ Ẑ*, i.e. h_0σ_∞(h_0) = 1, a Z/2-coboundary condition giving g_0.
Check of independence under λ → l_0^α λ (λ only defined in L_0\Π̂).

missed.claim: Grothendieck derives, before Drinfeld/Ihara, the GT-type defining equations as successive Z/3- and Z/2-cocycle conditions inside \widehat{PSL_2(Z)}. This is close to the later Lochak–Schneps 'cohomological interpretation of GT'. The parametrisation by two classes of order-3 elements (two forms (B)) suggests that two families of solutions are being tracked.
missed.quote: 1°) On choisit un ξ ∈ Π̂_{0,3} satisfaisant l'équation (A) ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ)=1 ... 2°) On choisit γ ∈ Ẑ tel que (C) σ_∞(ξ) = l_1^γ ξ^{-1} l_0^γ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority and documentation: a cohomological, torsion-element-based derivation of GT̂ in Grothendieck's own hand. The second branch ξ = λl_0^{-1}ρ(λ)^{-1} could be compared with the literature on GT̂ acting on \widehat{PSL_2(Z)}, where usually only conjugates of ρ are considered.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is a precursor of the Drinfeld/Ihara GT relations in an essentially cohomological form, matching later Lochak–Schneps work. It is historically interesting, but the mathematics is now well known and Grothendieck's GT-related ideas are partly documented.
transcription_corrections: (C) on this page clearly reads σ_∞(ξ) = l_1^γ ξ^{-1} l_0^γ (with ξ^{-1}), consistent with the derivation.

'Finalement, quand on change ou on change par la donnée du Π̂_{0,3}-conj. de ρ' probably reads 'Finalement, quand on change u en changeant ρ par ... Π̂_{0,3}-conj. de ρ'; the next line probably reads 'la démarche la plus claire pour déterminer tous ces u en question me semble celle-ci'.
'(sous la première soit sous la forme (55)...' probably reads '(on la prendra soit sous la forme (55), soit sous la forme (56))'.
'On devra donc dans (A) se borner aux ξ (pour t.q. aux λ)' probably reads 'On devra donc dans 1°) se borner aux ξ (resp. aux λ)'.
